G3400.def: a Roman mile, milliarium , = 1000 paces,= 8 stades, = 1680 yards, i. e. 80 yards less than our mile, (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

G3401.def:
μιμέομαι, -οῦμαι
(μῖμος, a mimic, an actor), [in LXX: Psaumes 31:6, Wis.4:2 15:9, 4Ma.9:23 4Mac 9:13 : * ;] 
to imitate: 2 Thessaloniciens 3:7 3:9 Hébreux 13:7, 3Jn.11.†

G3402.def:
μιμητής, -οῦ, ὁ
(μιμέομαι), 
in NT always (like the verb) in good sense, an imitator: 1 Corinthiens 4:16 11:1, Éphésiens 5:1, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:6 2:14, Hébreux 6:12.†

G3404.def:
μισέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׂנֵא ;] 
to hate: with accusative of person(s) Matthieu 5:43 24:10, Luc 1:71 6:22, 27 19:14, Jean 7:7 15:18-19, 23-26 17:14, Tite 3:3, 1 Jean 2:9 Jn 2:11 Jn 3:13 Jn 3:15 Jn 4:20 Apocalypse 17:16; pass., Matthieu 10:22 24:9, Marc 13:13, Luc 21:17; with accusative of thing(s), Jean 3:20, Romains 7:15, Éphésiens 5:29, Hébreux 1:9, Ju 23, Apocalypse 2:6; pass., Apocalypse 18:2. As the Heb. שָׂנֵא is sometimes found with the modified sense of indifference to or relative disregard for one thing in comparison with another (cf. Genèse 29:30-31, Deutéronome 21:15-16, Malachie 1:3) so prob. μ. in the foll.: Matthieu 6:24, Luc 14:26 16:13, Jean 12:25, Romains 9:13" (LXX) .†

G3405.def:
μισθαποδοσία, -ας, ἡ
(μισθός, ἀποδίδωμι; cl. μισθοδοσία), 
pay­ment of wages, recompense; meton., 
__(a) of reward: Hébreux 10:35 11:26; 
__(b) of punishment : Hébreux 2:2.†

G3406.def:
μισθ-απο-δότης, -ου, ὁ 
(see supr.), 
one who pays wages; meton., a rewarder: Hébreux 11:6.†

G3407.def:
μίσθιος, -α, -ον
(also -ος, -ον), [in LXX: Lévitique 19:13 A Lévitique 25:50, Job 7:1 (שָׂכִיר), Tob.5:11, Sir.7:10 31:22 37:11 * ;] 
hired; as subst., ὁ μ., a hired servant: Luc 15:17, 19 15:21 (Anth., Plut.).†

G3408.def:
μισθός, -οῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׂכָר ;] 
__1. prop., wages, hire: Matthieu 20:8, Luc 10:7, Romains 4:4, 1 Timothée 5:18, Jacques 5:4, Ju 11; μ. ἀδικίας, Actes 1:18, 2 Pierre 2:13 (but see Mayor and ICC, in l), 2 Pierre 2:15. 
__2. Generally, reward: Jean 4:36, 1 Corinthiens 9:18; esp. of divine rewards, Matthieu 5:12 6:1-2, 5 6:16 10:41-42 Marc 9:41, Luc 6:23, 35, 1 Corinthiens 3:8 3:14, 2Jn.8, Apocalypse 11:18 22:12; ἔχειν μ., Matthieu 5:46, 1 Corinthiens 9:17.†

G3409.def:
μισθόω, -ῶ
(μισθός) [in LXX (mid.) chiefly for שָׂכָר ;] 
to let out for hire. Mid., to hire: with accusative, Matthieu 20:1, 7.†

G3410.def:
μίσθωμα, -τος, τό
(μισθόω), [in LXX: Deutéronome 23:18 (19), Michée 1:7, Eze.16:31, 34 16:41 (אֶתְנַן), Eze.16:33, (נֵדֶה, נָדָן), Eze.16:32, Proverbes 19:13 * ;] 
__1. price, hire (cl, and LXX). 
__2. In sense not found elsewhere, a hired dwelling: Actes 28:30.†

G3411.def:
μισθωτός, -ή, όν 
(μισθόω), [in LXX for שָׂכִיר, Exode 12:45, al. ;] 
hired; as subst., ὁ μ., a hired servant, hireling: Marc 1:20, Jean 10:12-13.†

G3412.def:
Μιτυλήνη, -ης, ἡ
(late form - Strab., Plut. - of cl. Μυτιλ-), 
Mytilene, Mitylene, chief city of Lesbos: Actes 20:14.†

G3413.def:
Μιχαήλ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. מִיכָאֵל, who like God?), 
Michael, the Archangel (cf. Daniel 12:1) : Ju 9, Apocalypse 12:7.†

G3414.def:
μνᾶ, -ᾶς, ἡ
(a Semitic word; cf. Heb. מָנֶה, Aram. מְנֵא, a weight and a sum of money = 100 shekels, cf. 3Ki.10:17), 
a mina (Let.), mna, in Attic a weight and sum of money = 100 δραχμαί (which see) : Luc 19:13, 16 19:18, 20 19:24-25.†

G3417.def:
μνεία, -ας, ἡ
(μιμνήσκω), [in LXX for זָכַר, its parts and deriva­tives ;] 
remembrance, mention (= μνήμη) : Philippiens 1:3; μ. ποιεῖσθαι, with genitive of person(s), Romains 1:9, Éphésiens 1:16, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:2, Phm 4 (cf. Psaumes 111:4); μ. ἔχειν, with genitive of person(s), 1 Thessaloniciens 3:6, 2 Timothée 1:3 (on the seel. in Romains 12:13, see ICC, in I.; Field, Notes, 163).†

G3418.def:
μνῆμα, -τος, τό
(μνάομαι), [in LXX for קֶבֶר, קְבוּרָה ;] 
__1. a memorial. 
__2. a sepulchral monument, a sepulchre, tomb: Marc 5:3, 5 15:46 16:2 (WH, μνημεῖον), Luc 8:27 23:53 24:1, Actes 2:29 7:16, Apocalypse 11:9.†
SYN.: μνημεῖον

G3419.def:
μνημεῖον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX for קֶבֶר, קְבוּרָה ;] 
__1. a memorial, record (cl., cf. Wis.10:7). 
__2. (a) (cl.) a monument: Luc 11:47; 
__(b) a sepulchre, tomb (Genèse 23:6, 9, Ésaïe 22:16, al.): Matthieu 23:29, Marc 5:2, Luc 11:44, Jean 5:28, and frequently in Gospels, Actes 13:29 
SYN.: μνῆμα

G3420.def:
μνήμη, -ης, ἡ
(μνάομαι), [in LXX for זֵכֶר, זִכְרוֹן ;] 
memory, remembrance, mention: μ. ποιεῖσθαι, with genitive, to remember, 2 Pierre 1:15 (but in cl., π., μ. π. more frequently = to make mention, and so perh. here, cf. Mayor, in l; and for ex. from π., see Zorell, see word).†
SYN.: μνεία, q.v

G3421.def:
μνημονεύω
(μνήμων, mindful) [in LXX for זָכַר ;] 
__1. to call to mind, remember : absol., Marc 8:18; with genitive of person(s), Luc 17:32, Colossiens 4:18, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:3, Hébreux 11:15 (but see infr.) Hébreux 13:7; τ. πτωχῶν, Galates 2:20; with genitive of thing(s), Jean 15:20 16:4, 21, Actes 20:35; with accusative obj. (as more frequently in cl.), of persons, 2 Timothée 2:8; of things, Matthieu 16:9, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:9, Apocalypse 18:5; before ὅτι, Actes 20:31, Éphésiens 2:11, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:5; πόθεν, Apocalypse 2:5; πῶς, Apocalypse 3:3. 
__2. to make mention of: with genitive, Hébreux 11:15 (but see supr., and cf. M, Th., I, 18); before περί, Hébreux 11:22.†

G3422.def:
μνημόσυνον, -ου, τό
(μνήμων, mindful), [in LXX frequently for זֵכֶר, זִכְרוֹן and cogn. forms ;] 
a memorial: Matthieu 26:13, Marc 14:9, Actes 10:4 (where cf. Lévitique 2:9, 16 5:12, Num_5:28, Sir.45:16, al.).†

G3423.def:
μνηστεύω 
[in LXX for אָרַשׂ pi., pu. ;] 
__1. to woo and win, espouse. 
__2. to promise in marriage, betroth; pass., of the woman, to be be­trothed: with dative of person(s), Matthieu 1:18, Luc 1:27 2:5.†

G3424.def:
μογι-λάλος, -ον
(μόγις, λάλος), [in LXX: Ésaïe 35:6 (אִלֵּם) * ;] 
speaking with difficulty: Marc 7:32 (Tr., txt., μογγιλάλος, thick-voiced, see Swete, in l).†

G3425.def:
μόγις
adv. (μόγος, toil), [in LXX: Wis.9:16 א A (μόγις, B), 3Ma.7:6 * ;] 
with toil or difficulty, hardly: Luc 9:39 (μόγις, WH).†

G3426.def:
μοιχαλίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(= Att.. μοιχάς, fem. of μοιχός), [in LXX: Proverbes 18:22 30:20), Eze.16:38 23:45, Osée 3:1, Malachie 3:5 (נַאֲפוּף, נָאַף) * ;] 
an adulteress: Romains 7:3; meton., for μοιχεία, 2 Pierre 2:14. Metaphorical, of infidelity to God (cf. Eze.16:15 ff. Eze.23:43 ff., al.), Jacques 4:4; as an adj., Matthieu 12:39 16:4, Marc 8:8.†

G3428.def:
1. an adulteress , (New Testament):as adjective adulterous , (New Testament) 
2. as Substantive = μοιχεία, (New Testament) (ML)

G3429.def:
μοιχάω, -ῶ 
(= cl. μοιχεύω), [in LXX (mid., absol. and with accusative, with party of either sex as subj.) : Jérémie 3:8 5:7 7:9 9:2 23:14 29:23, Eze.16:32 23:37, 43 (נָאַף) * ;] 
to commit adultery with: with accusative, fem. In NT always mid, in same sense; of the man : absol., Matthieu 5:32 19:9 (WH, txt., R, mg., om.); before ἐπ᾽ αὐτήν, Marc 10:11; of the woman: Marc 10:12.†

G3430.def:
μοιχεία, -ας, ἡ
(μοιχύω), [rn LXX: Osée 2:2 (נַאֲפוּף), Osée 4:2 (נָאַף), Jérémie 13:27 (נִאֻף), Wis.14:26 * ;] 
adultery: Jean 8:3; pl. (see WM, 220; Bl., § 32, 6), Matthieu 15:19, Marc 7:21,†

G3431.def:
μοιχεύω
(μοιχός), [in LXX: Exode 20:13, Lévitique 20:10, al. (נָאַף) ;] 
to commit adultery: absol., Matthieu 5:27 19:18, Marc 10:19, Luc 16:18 18:20, Romains 2:22 13:9, Jacques 2:11; with accusative fem., Matthieu 5:28. Pass., of the woman, Matthieu 5:32 19:9 WH, mg.), Jean 8:4. Metaphorical, of idolatry (see: μιοιχαλίς, and cf. Jérémie 3:9, a1.), before μετ᾽ αὐτῆς, Apocalypse 2:22.†

G3432.def:
μοιχός, -οῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX for נָאַף ;] 
an adulterer: Luc 18:11, 1 Corinthiens 6:9, Hébreux 13:4.†

G3433.def:
μόλις 
adv. (μόλος, toil) 
post-Hom. alternative for μόγις, 
[in LXX: Proverbes 11:31, Wis.9:16, al. ;] 
with difficulty, hardly, scarcely: Luc 9:39 (T, μόγις), Actes 14:8 27:7-8, 16, Romains 5:7, 1 Pierre 4:18" (LXX) .†

G3434.def:
Μολόχ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. מֶלֶךְ, prop. מֶלֶךְ King, but vocalized to read בֺּשֶׁת, shame, of. Βάαλ, and see DB, iii, 415 f.), 
Moloch, the god of the Ammonites : Actes 7:43 (LXX).†

G3435.def:
μολύνω 
[in LXX: Genèse 37:31 (טָבַל), Ésaïe 59:3 (גָּאַל ni.), Zacharie 14:2 (שָׁכַב ni.), Sir.21:28, al. ;] 
to stain, soil, defile; in NT always symb. and figuratively: 1 Corinthiens 8:7, Apocalypse 3:4 14:4.†
SYN.: μιαίνω, q.v

G3436.def:
μολυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(μολύνω), [in LXX: Jérémie 23:15 (חֲנֻפָה), I Esther 8:83, 2Ma.5:27 * ;] 
defilement: with genitive obj., 2 Corinthiens 7:1 (Plut., FlJ).†

G3437.def:
μομφή, ῆς, ἡ
(μέμφομαι), 
poët. form of μέμψις, 
blame, com­plaint: Colossiens 3:13.†

G3439.def:
μονογενής, -ές
(μόνος, γένος), [in LXX: Juges 11:34, Psaumes 22:20 25:16 35:17 (יָחִיד), Tob.3:15 6:10, 14 8:17, Wis.7:22, Bar.4:16 * ;] 
only, only begotten (DCG, ii, 281), of sons and daughters : Luc 7:12 8:42 9:38, Hébreux 11:17; of Christ, Jean 3:16, 18, 1 Jean 4:9; μ. παρὰ πατρός, Jean 1:14; μ. θεός, Jean 1:18.†

G3440.def:
μόνον, see: μόνος.
μόνος, -η, -ον, 
[in LXX chiefly for לְבַד ;] 
__1. adj., alone, solitary, forsaken: with verb., Matthieu 14:23, Marc 6:47, Luc 9:36, al.; with pron., Matthieu 18:15, Marc 9:2, al.; with subst., Marc 9:8, Luc 4:8, al.; pleonast., οὐκ . . . εἰ μὴ μ., Matthieu 12:4, Luc 6:4, al.; attrib., only, (ὁ) μ. θεός, Jean 5:44 17:3, Romains 16:27, 1 Timothée 1:17, Ju 25. 
__2. As adv., 
__(a) neut., (μόνον, alone, only: referring to verb or predic., Matthieu 9:21, Marc 5:36, Jacques 1:22, al. (see Bl., §44, 2); οὐ (μὴ) μ., Galates 4:18, Jacques 1:22; οὐ μ. . . . ἀλλά (Bl, §77, 13.3), Actes 19:26, 1 Jean 5:6, al.; id. before καί (Bl., §81, 1.2), Romains 5:3 9:10, 2 Corinthiens 8:19, al.; 
__(b) κατὰ μόνας, alone (Bl., §44, 1), Marc 4:10, Luc 9:18.

G3441.def:
μόνος, -η, -ον, 
[in LXX chiefly for לְבַד ;] 
__1. adj., alone, solitary, forsaken: with verb., Matthieu 14:23, Marc 6:47, Luc 9:36, al.; with pron., Matthieu 18:15, Marc 9:2, al.; with subst., Marc 9:8, Luc 4:8, al.; pleonast., οὐκ . . . εἰ μὴ μ., Matthieu 12:4, Luc 6:4, al.; attrib., only, (ὁ) μ. θεός, Jean 5:44 17:3, Romains 16:27, 1 Timothée 1:17, Ju 25. 
__2. As adv., 
__(a) neut., (μόνον, alone, only: referring to verb or predic., Matthieu 9:21, Marc 5:36, Jacques 1:22, al. (see Bl., §44, 2); οὐ (μὴ) μ., Galates 4:18, Jacques 1:22; οὐ μ. . . . ἀλλά (Bl, §77, 13.3), Actes 19:26, 1 Jean 5:6, al.; id. before καί (Bl., §81, 1.2), Romains 5:3 9:10, 2 Corinthiens 8:19, al.; 
__(b) κατὰ μόνας, alone (Bl., §44, 1), Marc 4:10, Luc 9:18.

G3442.def:
μον-όφθαλμος, -ον
(μόνος), 
Ionic and κοινή, 
one-eyed, having one eye: Matthieu 18:9, Marc 9:47.†

G3443.def:
μονόω, -ῶ
(μόνος), [in Aq.: Genèse 49:6 ;] 
to leave alone, forsake: of a childless widow, pf. ptcp. pass., 1 Timothée 5:5.†

G3444.def:
μορφή, -ῆς, ἡ 
[in LXX: Juges 8:18 A (תֹּאַר), Job 4:16 (תְּמוּנָה), Ésaïe 44:13 (תַּבְנִית), Dan LXX 3:19 (צֶלֶם), Da TH Daniel 4:33 5:6, 9-10 7:28 (זִיו), Tob.1:13, Wis.18:1, 4Ma.15:4 * ;] 
form, shape, appearance (Hom., Eur., . sch., al.); in philos. lang. the specific character or essential form (Arist., see Gifford, Inc., 26 ff.) : Marc 16:12, Philippiens 2:6-7.†
SYN.: μόρφωσις, the outline, delineation, semblance of the μορφή, as distinct from the μ. itself (Lft., Notes, 262); σχῆμα, shape, fashion, disting. from μορφή as the outward and accidental from the inward and essential (cf. Tr., Syn., § LXX; Lft., Phi., 125 ff.; Gifford., Inc., l.with)

G3445.def:
μορφόω, -ῶ
(μορφή), [in Aq.: Ésaïe 44:13 * ;] 
to form: figuratively, Galates 4:19 (cf. μετα-, συμ-μορφόω)

G3446.def:
μόρφωσις, -εως, ἡ
(μορφόω), 
__1. a forming, shaping (Theophr.). 
__2. form, outline, semblance: Romains 2:20; opposite to δύναμις, 2 Timothée 3:5.†
SYN.: μορφή (which see), σχῆμα

G3447.def:
μοσχο-ποιέω, -ῶ 
to make a calf (as an image) : Actes 7:41 (LXX, ἐποίησε μόσχον).†

G3449.def:
μόχθος, -ου, ὁ
(= Hom. μόγος), in cl. chiefly poët., [in LXX for תְּלָאָה, עָמָל, etc. ;] 
toil, labour, hardship, distress: 2 Corinthiens 11:27, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:9, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:8.†
SYN.: κόπος (which see), πόνος

G3451.def:
μουσικός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX: Genèse 31:27, Eze.26:13 (שִׁיר), Dan LXX TH Daniel 3:5 ff. (זְמָר), Sir.22:6, al. ;] 
skilled in the arts, esp. in music; as subst., ὁ μ., a minstrel, musician: Apocalypse 18:22.†

G3452.def:
μυελός, -οῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX: Genèse 45:18 (חֶלֶב), Job 21:24 (מֹחַ) Job 33:24 * ;] 
marrow: Hébreux 4:12.†

G3453.def:
μυέω, -ῶ
(μύω, to shut the mouth), [in LXX: 3Ma.2:30 * ;] 
to initiate into the mysteries (so chiefly in cl.; LXX, l.with); hence, to instruct: pass., Philippiens 4:12 (RV, I have learned the secret).†

G3454.def:
μῦθος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Wis.17:4 A, Sir.20:19 * ;] 
__1. speech, con­versation. 
__2. (a) a story, narrative (Hom.); 
__(b) later, opposite to λόγος (a true narrative) = Lat. fabula, a myth, fable, fiction: 1 Timothée 1:4 4:7, 2 Timothée 4:4, Tite 1:14, 2 Pierre 1:16.†
SYN.. λόγος, q.v

G3455.def:
μυκάσμαι, -ῶμαι in cl. chiefly poët., 
[in Sm.: Job 6:5 * ;] 
prop., of oxen (onomatop.), to low, bellow; of a lion, to roar: Apocalypse 10:3.†

G3456.def:
μυκτηρίζω
(μυκτήρ, the nose), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:21, Job 22:19, Psaumes 80:6, al. (לָעַג), Proverbes 1:30 (נָאַץ) Proverbes 15:20 (בָּזָה), 1Ma.7:34, al. ;] 
to turn up the nose or sneer at, mock: pass., Galates 6:7 (cf. ἐκ-μυκτηρίζω).†

G3457.def:
μυλικός, -ή, -όν
(μύλη, a mill), 
of a mill: λίθος μ., Luc 17:2.†

G3458.def:
μύλος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX for רֵחֶה, Nombres 11:8, Deutéronome 24:6, al. ;] 
__1. = μύλη, a mill (Strab., Plut., LXX) : Matthieu 24:41, Apocalypse 18:22. 
__2. a mill-stone (Anth.) : Apocalypse 18:21 (T); μ. ὀνικός, Matthieu 18:6, Marc 9:42 (see Swete, in l).†

G3460.def:
Μύρα, Μύρρα (LT, Tr., WH), -ων, τά, 
Myra, a city of Lycia : Actes 27:5.†

G3461.def:
μυριάς, -άδος, ἡ
(μυρίος), [in LXX chiefly for רְבָבָה ;] 
ten thousand, a myriad: pl., Actes 19:19, Apocalypse 5:11 9:16; hyperb., of vast numbers, Luc 12:1, Actes 21:20, Hébreux 12:12, Ju 14.†

G3462.def:
μυρίζω
(μύρον), 
Ionic and poët. (comic), 
to anoint: Marc 14:8.†
SYN.: see: ἀλείφω, and cf. μύρον

G3463.def:
μυρίος, -α, -ον 
__1. numberless, countless, infinite: 1 Corinthiens 4:15 14:19. 
__2. As a definite numeral, in pl., μύριοι, -αι, -α, ten thousand: Matthieu 18:24.†

G3464.def:
μύρον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for שֶׁמֶן, Proverbes 27:9, Psaumes 133:2, al. ;] 
ointment: Matthieu 26:7, 12, Marc 14:3-5, Luc 7:37-38, 46 23:56, Jean 11:2 12:3, 5, Apocalypse 18:13.†
SYN.: ἔλαιον, q.v

G3465.def:
Μυσία, -ας, ἡ 
Mysia, a province of Asia Minor: Actes 16:7-8.†

G3466.def:
μυστήρισν, -ου, τό
(μυέω), [in LXX: Dan LXX TH Daniel 2:18 ff. (רָז), Tob.12:7, 11, Jdth.2:2, Wis.2:22 6:22 14:15, 23, Sir.3:18 22:22 27:16-17, 21, 2Ma.13:21 * ;] 
__1. that which is known to the μύστης (initiated), a mystery or secret doctrine, mostly in pl., τὰ μ. (Æsch., Hdt., al.). 
__2. In later writers (Menand., Incert., 168), that which may not be revealed (not, however, as in the modern sense, intrinsically difficult to understand), a secret or mystery of any kind (To, Jth, 2Mac, ll, with). 
__3. In NT, of the counsels of God (cf. Th.: Job 15:8, Psaumes 25:14 for סוֹד), once hidden but now revealed in the Gospel or some fact thereof; 
__(a) of the Christian revelation generally : Romains 16:25, 1 Corinthiens 2:7, Colossiens 1:26-27, Éphésiens 3:3, 9; τ. βασιλείας τ. θεοῦ, Marc 4:11; τ. θεοῦ, 1 Corinthiens 2:1, Apocalypse 10:7; τ. θ., Χριστοῦ, Colossiens 2:2; τ. Χριστοῦ., Colossiens 4:3, Éphésiens 3:4; τ. θελήματος αὐτοῦ, Éphésiens 1:9; τ. εὐαγγελίον, Éphésiens 6:19; τ. πίστεως, 1 Timothée 3:9; τ. εὐσεβείας, 1 Timothée 3:16; 
__(b) of particular truths, or details, of the Christian revelation : Romains 11:25, 1 Corinthiens 15:51, Éphésiens 5:32, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:7, Apocalypse 1:20 17:5, 7; pl., τὰ μ., 1 Corinthiens 13:2 14:2; θεοῦ, 1 Corinthiens 4:1; τ. βασιλείας τ. οὐρανῶν (θεοῦ), Matthieu 13:11, Luc 8:10 (cf. Westc., Eph., 180 ff.; AR, Eph., 234 ff.; Lft., Col., 165 f.; Hatch, Essays, 57 f.; DB, iii, 465 ff.; DCG, ii, 213 ff.).†

G3467.def:
μυ-ωπάζω
(μύωψ, closing the eyes, short-sighted; μύω, ὤψ) 
to be short-sighted: 2 Pierre 1:9 (R, mg., closing his eyes; see ICC, in l).†

G3468.def:
μώλωψ, -ωπος, ὁ 
[in LXX for חַבּוּרָה, Exode 21:25, al. ;] 
a bruise, wound from a stripe: 1 Pierre 2:24 (LXX) (Arist., Plut., al.).†

G3469.def:
μωμάομαι, -ῶμαι
(μῶμος), 
poët. and late prose, 
[in LXX: Proverbes 9:7 (מאוּם), Wis.10:14, Sir.31:18 * ;] 
to find fault with, blame: 2 Corinthiens 8:20; pass., 2 Corinthiens 6:3.†

G3470.def:
μῶμος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX, of physical blemishes : Lévitique 21:17 ff., Deutéronome 15:21, Cantique des cantiques 4:7, al. (מאוּם); of mental defect, Sir.20:24, al. ;] 
__1. in cl. poets and late prose, blame, disgrace. 
__2. In LXX, perb. because of resemblance to a physical blemish (cf. ἄμωμος, 1 Pierre 1:19, and see Hort., in l); metaphorically, of licentious persons, 2 Pierre 2:13.†

G3471.def:
μωραίνω
(μωρός), [in LXX: Ésaïe 19:11, Jérémie 10:14 51:17 (בָּעַר ni.), 2 Rois 24:10, Ésaïe 44:25 R (שָׂכַל ni., pi.)* ;] 
__1. cl., to be foolish, play the fool. 
__2. LXX and NT, causal, to make foolish: 1 Corinthiens 1:20; pass., to become foolish: Romains 1:22; of salt that has lost its flavour, become tasteless: Matthieu 5:13, Luc 14:34.†

G3472.def:
μωρία, -ας, ἡ
(μωρός), [in LXX: Sir.20:31 * ;] 
foolishness: 1 Corinthiens 1:18 1:21 1:23 2:14 3:19.†

G3474.def:
μωρός, -ά, -όν 
[in LXX for נָבָל, etc.; frequently in Sir. ;] 
__1. prop., of the nerves, dull, sluggish (Hipp., Arist.). 
__2. Of the mind, dull, stupid, foolish: Matthieu 5:22 (see Field, Notes, 3 ff.) Matthieu 7:26 23:17, 19 (T, WH, txt., R, om.) Matthieu 25:2-3, 8, 1 Corinthiens 3:18 4:10; of things, παράδοσις, Marc 7:13 (T, WH, txt., R, om.) : ζητήσεις, 2 Timothée 2:23, Tite 3:9; τὸ μ. τ. θεοῦ, 1 Corinthiens 1:25; τὰ μ. τ. κόσμου, 1 Corinthiens 1:27.†

G3475.def:
Μωυσῆς (Μωϋσῆς, T; Μωσῆς, Rec.), -έως, dative - (as LXX: Exode 5:20, al.), and -εῖ, accusative -ῆν (ac LXX) and -έα (Luc 16:29 only) (Heb. מֹשֶׁה), 
Moses: Matthieu 8:4 17:3-4, al.; νόμος Μωυσέως, Luc 2:22 24:44, Jean 7:23, Actes 13:39 15:5 28:23, 1 Corinthiens 9:9, Hébreux 10:28; by meton., of the books of Moses, Luc 16:29 24:27, Actes 15:21, 2 Corinthiens 3:15

G3476.def:
Ναασσών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נַחְשׁוֹן), 
Naasson: Matthieu 1:4, Luc 3:32.†

G3478.def:
Ναζαρά
(Matthieu 4:13­ L, -άθ­Luc 4:16) 
Ναζαρέθ (Matthieu 21:11, Actes 10:38), 
Ναζαρέτ (so always Rec.; WH, in foll, instances, where -έθ, T), ἡ, 
indecl. (Semitic form uncertain), 
Nazareth: Matthieu 2:23, Marc 1:9, Luc 1:26 2:4, 39 2:51, Jean 1:45-46.†

G3479.def:
Ναζαρηνός, -οῦ, ὁ 
(on the Semitic form, see Dalman, Gr., 141 n.) 
a Nazarene: Marc 1:24 10:47 14:67 16:6, Luc 4:34 24:19.†

G3480.def:
Ναζωραῖος, -ου, ὁ
(= -ρηνός, which see), 
a Nazarene: Matthieu 2:23 (LXX) Matthieu 26:71, Luc 18:37, Jean 18:5, 7 19:19, Actes 2:22 3:6 4:10 6:14 22:8 24:5 26:9.†

G3481.def:
Ναθάμ (Rec. Ναθάν), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נָתַן), 
Nathan: Luc 3:31.†

G3482.def:
Ναθαναήλ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נְתַנְאֵל), 
Nathaniel, prob. to be identified with Bartholomew (which see): Jean 1:45-49 21:2.†

G3483.def:
ναί 
particle of affirmation, 
yea, verily, even so; in answer to a question: Matthieu 9:28 13:51 17:25 21:16, Jean 11:27 21:15-16, Actes 5:8 22:27, Romains 3:29; before λέγω ὑμῖν, Matthieu 11:9, Luc 7:26; repeated for emphasis, ναὶ ναί (opposite to oὒ oὔ): Matthieu 5:37; ἤτω ὑμῶν τὸ ναὶ ναί, Jacques 5:12; ν. καὶ οὔ, 2 Corinthiens 1:18-19; ἵνα ᾖ . . . τὸ ναὶ ναί, 2 Corinthiens 1:17; τὸ ν., 2 Corinthiens 1:20; in assent to an assertion: Matthieu 15:27, Marc 7:28, Apocalypse 14:13 16:7; in confirmation of a previous assertion: Matthieu 11:26, Luc 10:21 11:51 12:5, Philippiens 4:3, Phm 20; in solemn asseveration Apocalypse 1:7 22:20.†

G3484.def:
Ναίν (Rec. Ναΐν), ἡ, indecl. (Heb. נָאָה), 
Nain, a village of Galilee: Luc 7:11.†

G3485.def:
ναός, -οῦ, ὁ 
(Att.. νεώς; ναίω, to inhabit), [in LXX (νεώς, 2Ma.6:2, al.) chiefly for הֵיכָל ;] 
__1. a temple (Hom., Find., al.). 
__2. The inmost part of a temple, the shrine (Hat., Xen., al.); in NT, 
__(a) generally: pl., Actes 17:24; of silver models of a heathen shrine, Actes 19:24; 
__(b) of the temple building proper, or sanctuary, at Jerusalem, as distinct from τ. ἱερόν (which see), the whole temple enclosure: Matthieu 23:16-17, 35 27:5, 40, Marc 14:58 15:29 Jean 2:19-20, Apocalypse 11:2; (τοῦ) θεοῦ, Matthieu 26:61 27:51, Marc 15:38, Luc 1:9, 21-22 23:45, 1 Corinthiens 3:17, 2 Corinthiens 6:16, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:4, Apocalypse 11:1; of the temple in the Apocal. visions, Apocalypse 3:12 7:15 11:19 14:15, 17 15:5-6, 8 16:1, 17 21:22 a. Metaphorical, of Christians, 1 Corinthiens 3:16 6:19, 2 Corinthiens 6:16, Éphésiens 2:21; of Christ's body, Jean 2:21 (cf. Jean 2:19); ὁ θεὸς ν. αὐτῆς ἐστιν, Apocalypse 21:22 b.†
SYN.: ἱερόν

G3486.def:
Ναούμ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נַחוּם;), 
Nahum: Luc 3:25.†

G3488.def:
the narcissus , (Homeric Hymns), etc. 
From ναρκάω, because of its narcotic properties. (ML)

G3489.def:
ναυαγέω, -ῶ
(ναῦς, + ἄγνυμι, to break) 
to suffer shipwreck: 2 Corinthiens 11:25; metaphorically, before περὶ τ. πίστιν, 1 Timothée 1:19.†

G3490.def:
ναύ-κληρος, -ου, ὁ
(ναῦς, κλῆρος), 
a shipowner, shipmaster: Actes 27:11.†

G3491.def:
ναῦς, νεώς accusative ναῦν, ἡ, 
[in LXX for עָנִי, אֲנִיָּה ;] 
a ship: Actes 27:41 (elsewhere in NT always τ. πλοῖον; see M, Proverbes 25:1-28 f.; Bl., Gosp., 186 f.).†

G3492.def:
ναύτης, -ου, ὁ
(ναῦς), [in Aq.: Eze.27:9; Sm.: Eze.27:29 * ;] 
a seaman, sailor: Actes 27:27, 30, Apocalypse 18:17.†

G3493.def:
Ναχώρ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נָחוֹר), 
Nahor: Luc 3:34.†

G3494.def:
νεανίας, -ου, ὁ
(νεάν = νέος) [in LXX for נַעַר, בָּחוּר ;] 
a young man: Actes 7:58 20:9 23:17-18.†

G3495.def:
νεανίσκος, -ου, ὁ
(dimin. of νεανίας) [in LXX chiefly for נַעַר, also for בָּחוּר, etc. ;] 
a young man, youth: Matthieu 19:20, 22, Marc 14:51 16:5, Luc 7:14, Actes 2:17" (LXX) Actes 23:18, 22, 1 Jean 2:13-14; of an attendant (cf. Genèse 14:24, al.) : Actes 5:10.†

G3497.def:
Ναιμάν (Rec. Νεεμάν), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נַעֲמָן), 
Naaman: Luc 4:27.†

G3498.def:
νεκρός, -α, -ον, 
[in LXX chiefly for מֵת ;] 
dead, 
__I. as adj., 
__1. prop.: Actes 5:10 20:9, Jacques 2:26, Apocalypse 1:18, al.; ὡσεὶ ν., Matthieu 28:4, Marc 9:26, Apocalypse 1:17; of that which is subject to death, Romains 8:10. 
__2. Metaphorical, 
__(a) of persons: Luc 15:24, 32; of those immersed in worldly cares, Matthieu 8:22, Luc 9:60; of spiritual death, Jean 5:25, Romains 6:13, Éphésiens 5:14, Apocalypse 3:1; τ. παραπτώμασιν, Éphésiens 2:1, 5 Colossiens 2:13; of the opposite condition, ν. τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, Romains 6:11; 
__(b) of things regarded as inoperative, devoid of power: ἁμαρτία, Romains 7:8; πίστις, Jacques 2:17, 26; ἔργα, Hébreux 6:1 9:14. 
__II. As subst., νεκρός, ὁ (Hom., al.), chiefly in pl. (οἱ) ν., the dead: Matthieu 11:5, Marc 12:26, Luc 20:37, 1 Corinthiens 15:15, al.; ἀνάστασις (τ.) νεκρῶν, Matthieu 22:31, Actes 17:32, al.; ν. . . . ζῶντες, Matthieu 22:32, Marc 12:27, Actes 10:42, al.; ἀπὸ νεκρῶν, Luc 16:30; ἐκ ν., Marc 6:14, Luc 24:46, Jean 12:1, Actes 13:34, Romains 10:7, al.; πρωτότοκος ἐκ τῶν ν., Colossiens 1:18; ζωὴ ἐκ ν., Romains 11:15; constr. praegn., ἐκ ν. ζῶντες, Romains 6:13.

G3499.def:
νεκρόω, ῶ
(νεκρός), 
to make dead, put to death; pass., to be dead: hyperbolically, of impotent age, Hébreux 11:12; σῶμα, Romains 4:19. Trop., of carnal impulses, τὰ μέλη, Colossiens 3:5.†
